extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, JPO examiners, and IP office stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes the Japan Patent Office's evaluation criteria, operational targets, quality principles, and procedural/legislative changes relevant to patent examination and prosecution. Includes timeliness targets, quality tenets, guidance updates, cooperative programs, and legal/fee reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency targets for accelerated examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Targets for accelerating examination: First Action Pendency — 10 months or less (targeted for FY2023); Standard Total Pendency* — 14 months or less (targeted for FY2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: *“Standard Total Pendency” excludes cases in which the JPO requests applicants to respond to second notices of reasons for refusal, for example. The accelerated examination sequence emphasized: Request for examination → First Action → Granting patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent quality tenets: robust, broad, valuable
rubrics_metrics.description: The 3 main tenets of patent quality are: 'robust' (so as not to be invalidated afterward), 'broad' (coverage matching the technical level of inventions and their disclosures), and 'valuable' (so as to be recognized around the world).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles are presented as the foundational criteria for granting high-quality patents; examinations should aim to produce patents meeting all three aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality management system enhancements
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhancement of Quality Management System including appointment of Quality Management Officers and conducting quality reviews by the Subcommittee on Examination Quality Management (a committee of external experts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since April 2014 the JPO appointed 90 Quality Management Officers; quality reviews are an explicit mechanism to manage and assure examination quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete update and clarity of Examination Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive update of Examination Guidelines to make descriptions more clear and concise and enable them to be accepted globally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines were revised to improve understandability and international acceptability; this is intended to improve predictability in obtaining patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensuring highly capable human resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing various career paths and training suited to the level of each examiner to ensure highly capable human resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human resource development and career pathing are explicit quality measures to maintain examiner capability and consistency in examination quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective examination of IP portfolios aligned with business strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Team examiners in specific technology fields collaboratively examine corporate IP portfolios in line with corporate business activities and business strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective examination involves grouping examiners by technology to consider manufacturing, components, designs, trademarks, etc., so examination reflects business strategy and portfolio-level considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: US‑JP Collaborative Search Pilot Program (US‑JP CSP) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Under US‑JP CSP, JPO and USPTO examiners each conduct prior art searches and share search results and opinions; they notify applicants of their First Office Actions around the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program aims to provide applicants earlier, contemporaneous, stronger and more stable patent rights. Process steps: request for CSP → sharing search results/opinions → contemporaneous First Office Actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) participation and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the PPH to accelerate prosecution: the JPO initiated PPH with the U.S. in 2006; participation has expanded to many offices (39 listed) and the number of PPH requests has steadily increased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistics and growth are used as evidence of effectiveness; note that over 90% of worldwide patent applications (2011) were filed in countries/regions participating in PPH-program countries/regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global work‑sharing tools and dossier linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: Advancing global work sharing through One Portal Dossier (OPD), WIPO-CASE, and linkage of OPD and WIPO-CASE to share dossiers beyond IP5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes participating offices (JPO, EPO, USPTO, KIPO, SIPO), scale (~160,000 applications annually, >440,000 accesses annually), and the goal of global work-sharing via dossier exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraging employee inventions (statutory change)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative revision to make it possible for employers to have the right to obtain a patent when the right becomes effective, while giving employees the right to receive incentives that are basically the same as those under the current Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change alters entitlement structures for employee inventions; it is presented as a policy to encourage utilization of inventions within companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revising patent and trademark fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Revision of patent/trademark fees: decreasing patent fees by 10%, decreasing trademark registration fees by 25%, and decreasing trademark renewal fees by 20%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee reductions are a policy lever to encourage filings and use of IP rights; they are part of recent legal reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accession to the Patent Law Treaty (PLT) and procedural flexibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceding to the PLT to allow extra time for applicants to submit translations when they were unable to submit within prescribed deadlines and to permit certain corrections (e.g., submit missing documents) for a certain period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedural flexibilities reduce harsh procedural forfeitures and align JPO practice with international standards to help applicants preserve rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and update points of Examination Guidelines/Handbooks
rubrics_metrics.description: The updated documents include: Examination Guidelines (summarize basic ideas of applying laws), Examination Handbook (summarizes essential points and provides sufficient examples and court precedents), and Handbook for PCT procedures (details practices for JPO acting as ISA/IPEA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update points emphasized: making descriptions clearer and more concise; providing enough case examples and court precedents in the Handbook; making the Guidelines internationally acceptable — all intended to improve user understanding and predictability of obtaining patent rights.
